text:
### Observed differences

- Activities A01 and A02 disappear: in the earlier window each took part in about 50 of 100 traces (roughly one occurrence per participating trace, with repeats in about 23 of 100), while in the later window neither is observed at all (0 of 200 traces), and their outgoing edges (A01 to A07/A10/A08/A12, A02 to A14) are gone. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002]
- Activity A09, not observed earlier, appears in the later window in about 24 of 100 traces and leads to A11 (about 46 of 100 outgoing transitions) or A12 (about 44 of 100). [OCC009, DIR007, POS007, REL065]
- A06 is repeated far less and re-routed: earlier it occurred about twice per trace overall (about four times per trace containing it, repeated in about 39 of 100 traces) and led to A13 (about 51 of 100) or A02 (about 49 of 100); in the later window it occurs about 0.5 times per trace (about 36 of 100 traces, rarely repeated) and every observed outgoing transition goes to A14. [OCC006, DIR004, LAG014]
- A14 changed successor: earlier it always led to A01; in the later window it leads to A08 (about 56 of 100), A07 (about 35 of 100) and A12 or A09 (about 8 of 100), and it sits earlier in the trace (mean position about 0.55 to 0.45). [DIR011, POS012, LAG043]
- A08 and A10 changed from alternatives to a fixed sequence: earlier they never shared a trace (A08 in about 24 of 100, A10 in about 26 of 100, with A08 always followed by A05); in the later window both occur in about 50 of 100 traces, A08 is always followed by A10, the pair co-occurs with A08 first in half the traces, and A05 now follows A08 two steps later instead of immediately. [OCC008, OCC010, DIR006, REL059, LAG023]
- A13 re-attached: earlier it led back to A06 (about 98 of 100 outgoing) and repeated within traces (mean 1.0 per trace); in the later window it always leads to A14, occurs less often (mean about 0.4, about 28 of 100 traces), and A04 now leads to A13 in about 39 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (earlier about 99 of 100 went to A06). [DIR010, DIR003, OCC013, LAG041, LAG006]
- A07 and A12 now route to the new activity about half the time: A07 earlier led to A12 in about 92 of 100 outgoing transitions, later to A12 (about 46) or A09 (about 48); A12 earlier led to A11 in about 95 of 100, later to A11 (about 54) or A09 (about 42). [DIR005, DIR009]
- Distances shrink where A01/A02 used to sit: A04 reaches A14 in exactly 2 steps in the later window (earlier typically 3–5 steps), A06 reaches A08 in 2 steps (earlier 4), A13 reaches A08 and A10 in 2 and 3 steps (earlier 5), A06 reaches A14 immediately in about 74 of 100 pairs (earlier at 2 or more steps), and A04 is now always immediately followed by A06. [LAG007, LAG010, LAG038, LAG039, LAG014, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the control flow around the A06–A14 core was re-routed: A01 and A02 (previously each in about half of all traces) are no longer executed, so A06 leads directly to A14 instead of to A02 or back to A13; A14 distributes to A08, A07, A12 and the newly appearing A09 instead of to A01; A08 continues into A10 (previously A05), turning A08 and A10 from mutually exclusive alternatives into a sequence; and A13, now reachable directly from A04, closes into A14 instead of back into A06. With the old cycles through A02–A14–A01 and A13–A06 gone, A06 and A13 repeat far less often (A06 about four occurrences per containing trace earlier versus about 1.4 later). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC006, OCC009, OCC013, DIR003, DIR004, DIR006, DIR010, DIR011, REL059, LAG007, LAG014, LAG041]

The supporting signs are direct and mutually consistent: the participation changes rest on 99 versus 0 traces (A01, A02) and 0 versus 47 traces (A09); the rewiring is observed directly in the successor profiles, and the relation and lag evidence agrees with it (A08/A10 from never co-occurring to always co-occurring in order; A04→A14 shortening from 3–5 steps to exactly 2), so the items describe one coherent re-routing rather than isolated shifts. The key items all exceed about 199 of 200 random re-split differences. [OCC001, OCC009, DIR004, DIR011, REL059, LAG007, LAG010]

Limitations: the evidence contains no screening baseline, so the number of chance findings could not be compared and the judgement rests on the size, directness and consistency of the differences. The evidence cannot show whether the re-routing was abrupt or completed gradually before the later window, and a shift in the mix of case types (for example, only a subpopulation previously using the A01/A02 loop) would look the same in these aggregates. Many relation items involving A01 and A02 restate the same disappearance and are not independent confirmations. [OCC001, OCC002, REL001, REL013]

Other differences: A07, A11 and A12 occur slightly less often per trace (mean about 0.48 to 0.40) while their participation stays near 23 of 100 traces, A14's per-trace mean drops slightly (about 0.98 to 0.90), and A06, A08 and A10 sit somewhat earlier in the trace; these small shifts are consistent with the re-routing above rather than separate changes. [OCC007, OCC011, OCC012, OCC014, POS004, POS006, POS008, POS012]
